props.name: The distorted five-membered ring at the single-atom vacancy is the catalytic site for CO2 activation

evidence.quote: A catalytic site is formed that favours the adsorption and activation of CO2.

props.statement: Differential charge density shows that at a single-atom vacancy the electron population accumulates on the carbon-deficient side, forming a distorted five-membered carbon ring; this site favours the adsorption and activation of CO2.

props.name: Single B doping lowers the overpotential only modestly

evidence.quote: the overpotential of BPC (1.27 eV) is lower than that of pristine graphene (2.20 eV). However, the improvement in the catalytic activity with single-B-atom doping is still very limited.

props.statement: Single-B-atom doping creates no structural defect but an electron-deficient centre; it only slightly increases the electron population at the Fermi level and lowers the overpotential modestly (BPC 1.27 eV vs pristine graphene 2.20 eV), so the improvement is limited.

props.name: Barely any synergistic effect between O and B in BPC-O

evidence.quote: The overpotential of the ECO2RR on BPC-O is 1.28 eV, meaning that there is barely any synergistic effect between the doped O and B atoms.

props.statement: BPC-O adsorbs H more strongly but does not catalyse ECO2RR better than BPC; its overpotential (1.28 eV) is essentially that of BPC, showing barely any synergistic effect between the doped O and B atoms.

props.name: CO desorption rate-limits and poisons void-graphene

evidence.quote: The strong adsorption of CO on the void defect site prevents it from being released and leads to catalyst poisoning at room temperature, which cannot be compensated even under a higher applied potential.

props.statement: On void-graphene the interaction with the product CO is very strong (desorption energy 2.29 eV), CO desorption becomes rate-limiting, and the strong CO adsorption on the void defect site leads to catalyst poisoning at room temperature.

props.name: A single-atom vacancy promotes ECO2RR activity more than a multiatom vacancy

evidence.quote: a single-atom vacancy defect is able to promote the ECO2RR activity of graphene more signiﬁcantly than a vacancy defect formed by multiple missing atoms

props.statement: A single-atom vacancy defect promotes the ECO2RR activity of graphene more significantly than a vacancy formed by multiple missing atoms, because it interacts more strongly with CO2 (Ead from −1.48 to −0.64 eV on the void catalysts, all higher than −0.20 eV on the hole catalysts).

props.name: ECO2RR on pristine graphene follows the single-molecule Eley-Rideal mechanism

evidence.quote: Therefore, the CO2 reduction reaction on pristine graphene follows the single molecular Eley–Rideal (ER) mechanism.

props.statement: Because CO2 adsorbs very weakly and atomic H adsorption is thermodynamically unfavourable on pristine graphene, the CO2 reduction follows the single-molecule Eley-Rideal (ER) mechanism.

props.name: ECO2RR on void-graphene follows the single-molecule ER mechanism

evidence.quote: Hence, the reduction reaction on the void-graphene surface follows the single molecule ER mechanism.

props.statement: On void-graphene atomic H competes with CO2 for the same adsorption site and adsorbs more weakly, so the reduction follows the single-molecule Eley-Rideal mechanism.

props.name: No catalytic synergy between N and B in hole-NBPC

evidence.quote: This overpotential is only 0.06 eV lower than that of hole-NPC, conﬁrming that the doped N plays a critical role in the activity of hole-NBPC and that there is no catalytic synergy effect between N and B.

props.statement: In hole-NBPC the N atom is separated from B by two carbon atoms; its overpotential (0.99 eV) is only 0.06 eV lower than that of hole-NPC, so the doped N plays the critical role and there is no catalytic synergy effect between N and B.

props.name: ECO2RR on hole-NPC follows the bimolecular LH mechanism

evidence.quote: the reduction reaction follows the bimolecular LH mechanism to produce the intermediate *COOH

props.statement: On hole-NPC atomic H adsorbs on the pyridinic N while CO2 stays in the resting state, so the reduction to *COOH follows the bimolecular Langmuir-Hinshelwood mechanism.

props.name: ECO2RR on void-NPC follows the bimolecular Langmuir-Hinshelwood mechanism

evidence.quote: the CO2 reduction reaction follows the bimolecular adsorption Langmiur-Hinshelwood (LH) mechanism.

props.statement: Because CO2 and atomic H adsorb on different sites of void-NPC (CO2 at the single-carbon defect, H on pyridinic N), the reduction follows the bimolecular adsorption Langmuir-Hinshelwood mechanism.

props.name: Pyridinic N is the atomic-H adsorption site and facilitates proton transfer

evidence.quote: Clearly, N doping greatly enhances the adsorption of H on the catalyst surface and facilitates the combination of atomic hydrogen and CO2 as a proton in the subsequent reduction reaction.

props.statement: Pyridinic N doping barely changes CO2 adsorption but provides the site for atomic H adsorption; the polar N-H bond it forms strongly polarizes H and facilitates proton transfer in the CO2→*COOH reduction step.

props.name: Single N doping improves activity more than single B doping

evidence.quote: single N-doping is able to improve the catalytic activity of the graphene-based catalyst to a higher extent than single B atom doping, which is consistent with the experiments

props.statement: Single N doping improves the catalytic activity of graphene-based catalysts to a higher extent than single B atom doping, consistent with experiment.

props.name: N and B codoping acts synergistically through a B-O bond with CO2 and *COOH

evidence.quote: Hence, the existence of B could further enhance the interaction between the catalyst and the reactant CO2 captured by the defect resulting from N-doping.

props.statement: Codoping B with N works synergistically: the electron-deficient B atom forms a B-O bond with the reactant CO2 and with the *COOH intermediate captured by the void defect from N doping, strengthening their interaction and promoting the first reduction step (CO2→*COOH) to a spontaneous process (−0.37 eV) on void-NBPC.

props.name: O doping fills the empty level above the Fermi level and weakens CO back-bonding

evidence.quote: in void-NBPC-O, this virtual energy level vanishes because the excess electrons brought by the doped oxygen ﬁll it, which in turn weakens the interaction between the catalyst and CO and facilitates the release of the product.

props.statement: In void-NBPC an empty level 0.12 eV above the Fermi level accepts electrons from CO (back-donation); in void-NBPC-O this virtual level vanishes because the excess electrons of the doped O fill it, which weakens the catalyst-CO interaction, makes CO desorption spontaneous and circumvents CO poisoning.

props.name: The potential-determining step generally lies in the first reduction step

evidence.quote: In general, the potential determining step in the reaction lies in the ﬁrst reduction reaction.

props.statement: Across the catalysts studied, the potential-determining step of the ECO2RR (CO2→*COOH→*CO→CO) generally lies in the first reduction step.

props.name: The single-atom vacancy defect activates CO2 and promotes catalytic activity

evidence.quote: Evidently, the void defect on graphene is able to activate CO2 molecules and remarkably promote the catalytic activity of the catalyst.

props.statement: The void (single-atom vacancy) defect activates adsorbed CO2 (bent, charged) and remarkably promotes the catalytic activity of graphene.

props.name: void-NBPC is excluded as an efficient CO2-to-CO catalyst by CO poisoning

evidence.quote: this result practically excludes void-NBPC as an efficient catalyst to selectively reduce CO2 to CO.

props.statement: Although void-NBPC promotes both reduction steps, the product CO interacts very strongly with it (Ead −2.16 eV; desorption free energy 1.51 eV, rate-limiting); the adsorbed CO poisons the catalyst or is further reduced to side products, which practically excludes void-NBPC as an efficient catalyst for the selective reduction of CO2 to CO.

props.name: void-NBPC-O has the best overall ECO2RR performance of the catalysts studied

evidence.quote: This result indicates that void-NBPC-O has the best performance on the whole catalytic reaction among all the catalysts studied in this work and circumvents CO poisoning.

props.statement: void-NBPC-O (N/B/O-codoped graphene with a single-atom vacancy) shows the best performance over the whole catalytic reaction among all catalysts studied, with an overpotential of 0.64 eV at the equilibrium potential (U = −0.89 V operating), and circumvents CO poisoning.
